main_text.p: Chaldaica lingua affinis Hebraica.¶CHALDAICA lingua, quæ & Aramæa, & Syrorum, & Assyriorum, & Babyloniorum vocatur, hodie eruditiores in Ægypto & Æthiopiâ utuntur, ut audio: Hebraicæ confinis est: nec fortè multò amplius differt quàm Dorica à Græca communi.

head.i: Oratio Dominica in lingua Syriaca vel Chaldæa, ex Evangelio Matthæi, Viennæ impresso.

main_text.p: Abun debaschmajá.iith kaddásch schemóch, tithé malcuthóth. jehee tzebjonóch echàn-na debaschmajá aph bearhá, hablan lachme desunkanàn jomona . uschbúck lan cho-boin eichana deaph hhanun schebakan lech iaboin.Vela tahalan lenifajona ella phatzan men bischa . Methil dediloch hi malcutha, vechaila,verthaschbuch thá lehalám almin.

Hac linguâ utuntur hodie in sacris & grammaticis (alioqui vulgaris sermo Arabicus his est:) quamplurimi Christiani; qui in tota Syria habitant, sed præcipuè circa montem Libanum, ad quatuor millia hominum: vulgò Christianos de Zona dicunt. Chaldaicos in ripa repertos characteres à transitu fluminis notant.

page.notes: The left marginal note is printed as three lines with hyphens at the breaks ("af-finis", "He-braica"); I joined them. Sentence-initial V in "Vela" and "vechaila" is read as a consonant as printed. "lan cho-boin" is a line-end break, hyphen kept. "iaboin.Vela" has no space in print, kept as is. The "Viennæ impresso" line is read with some uncertainty.
